text:
Anthropic just destroyed all proactive agent startups. 

That's what you'll see on your timeline. 

That couldn't be further from the truth.

Personal agents, unlike other agent types, will exist in different flavors and personalities. 

It's nice that Claude Duet runs on Opus 5.5. 

Unlike other agent types, people will really think carefully about which personal agent to pick. Here, people think more carefully about trust, personality, intent understanding, continual learning, etc. The best personal agent is the one you can trust, not just the fastest one that gets the work done effectively. 

But I think people will use multiple personal agents for different types of tasks/work. I think we are about to see an explosion of vertical personal agents. 

Which one do I use? I am still testing a bunch of them (dots, Muse, and Grok Bot). But I have actually just built my own with Pi Durable. I like mine better because it is hyper-personalized to how I use personal agents.

OpenAI just made long-running AI agents a lot cheaper.

As of yesterday, the Responses API can keep your prompt cache for 12 hours. It used to be 30 minutes.

Why it matters: an agent that runs all day sends the same instructions, tools and docs over and over. Before, any pause over 30 minutes meant paying full price for all of it.

The numbers (GPT-5.6 and newer):
→ Cached input costs 10x less, 20x less on GPT-6.1 Sol
→ Writing a 12-hour cache costs 2.5x the normal input rate
→ It beats no caching from the 3rd reuse

For an agent that runs once an hour on GPT-6.1 Sol, that's roughly 75% cheaper.

Codex lead Tibo also says Codex and Work now keep your cache forever, so coming back to an old thread doesn't start from zero.

One catch most people miss: the cache only matches the start of your prompt. Change one word at the top and the discount is gone.

So build every agent prompt in this order:
1. System instructions (never change)
2. Tools and docs (rarely change)
3. Examples
4. Conversation history
5. The new message (always last)

Keep timestamps, user names and random IDs out of the top.

How much of your API bill is the same prompt sent twice?

OpenAI's prompt caching guide: http://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching

text:
This Christmas side hustle is going viral with fake math. The real numbers are still worth it.

10 x $5 is $50. You'd need 300 sales.

The idea is still good, though. A digital coloring book costs almost nothing to make, and parents buy them every December.

Here's how I'd actually do it.

1. Plan it in Claude:
"Plan a 30-page Christmas coloring book for kids ages 4-8. Give me a title and 30 page ideas, one simple scene per page. Original characters only, no brands or movie characters. Mix easy pages with a few detailed ones."

2. Draw it in ChatGPT Images (Claude doesn't make images):
"Black and white coloring page for kids. Thick clean outlines, no shading, no gray, white background. Scene: [page idea]. Portrait, letter size."

3. Write the listing in Claude:
"Write a Gumroad listing for this book: [title + page list]. Title under 60 characters, 3 short bullets on what parents get, the age range, and one line on printing at home."

Then put the pages into one PDF in Canva and upload it.

What would you sell for under $10 this Christmas?
